c_O5SPsrTISNsP-k9wnEpw.title: Women Building Europe Together Forum
c_O5SPsrTISNsP-k9wnEpw.description: The closing public event of the Bridges of Empowerment project by the Union of Ukrainian Women in Greece: a workshop, self-presentations and networking.
c_O5SPsrTISNsP-k9wnEpw.content:
How can we turn our experience, skills and connections into economic and civic opportunities? An evening for women who are building their future in Greece and creating a stronger community together.

**Where:** Glyfada Old Town Hall, Saki Karagiorga 4, Glyfada 166 75.

**Programme**

- Workshop: Lesia Rimovych (real estate and investment) — “Visibility: how to make your work seen and open up new opportunities”; Yana Pavlova (coach and mentor for women) — “10 tips to get your products and services valued”.
- Self-presentations: five minutes to tell everyone about yourself, your business or your project (mention this in the registration form).
- Networking with colour-coded badges: career, business, partnership or community support.
- An “I offer”, “I’m looking for”, “Let’s create together” board.

Organised by the Union of Ukrainian Women in Greece. The project is supported by a RIZA grant and the European Union. Register via the link in the [organisers’ post](https://www.facebook.com/ukrainianwomengr).

fzkVW0JpQHCNF6Ov2Vn1MQ.content:
The course lasts ten weeks and starts from scratch. Classes take place twice a week in the evening, so people who work can come too.
The teacher is a Ukrainian woman who has lived in Greece for more than ten years. The focus is on everyday language: documents, the doctor, school, renting a flat, a job interview.
During classes there is a children’s room with volunteers, so you can come along with your kids.

HI06q1w8Sgm17iPk4vjJAA.title: “Ukraine by Hand”: Yavoriv painting
HI06q1w8Sgm17iPk4vjJAA.description: The first workshop in the series: the story of the tradition, brushes, colours and your own Yavoriv bird. Plus a Yavoriv pie to taste.
HI06q1w8Sgm17iPk4vjJAA.content:
Some traditions are not just for remembering. You can make them with your own hands.

Join us for the first meeting of the “Ukraine by Hand” series: an introduction to Yavoriv painting, a folk art from western Ukraine. We’ll talk about the history of the tradition, pick up brushes and colours, and each paint our own Yavoriv bird. And we’ll taste a Yavoriv pie, so the evening is as delicious as it is creative.

**Where:** 4 Feron Street, Athens. **Duration:** 2.5 hours. **Price:** €28, all materials included.

No painting experience needed. Places are limited — it’s a small, hands-on workshop. Send us the word “BIRD” in a Direct message for details and registration.

SqS8pzlTT4SAwYFYVM4Xxg.title: Icon painting school in Athens — third session
SqS8pzlTT4SAwYFYVM4Xxg.description: Paint a real icon in 10 days. All materials are provided; at the end, the icons are blessed and you receive a certificate.
SqS8pzlTT4SAwYFYVM4Xxg.content:
The Ukrainian church community of St Nicholas, with the support of the Trembita Society for the Support and Development of Cultural Heritage, invites everyone interested in sacred art.

**Paint an icon yourself!** Anyone can give it a try — practically every participant manages to complete an icon. In 10 days you’ll create a sacred image with your own hands — a real icon that will stay with you for life.

After a shared Divine Liturgy, the priests will bless the icons as the fruit of ten days of work and prayer. Every participant receives a certificate of completion from Trembita and the community.

**Donation:** €170 per person — this covers all materials (boards, paints, brushes, gold leaf, pencils and everything else you need). Places are limited.

**Registration and information:** Fr Ihor — +30 690 787 4857, Oksana — +30 699 369 3397, Olena — +30 694 920 6258.

T-VVxB_kS7GVYYmbcabIIw.title: How to enrol your child in a Greek school: a step-by-step guide
T-VVxB_kS7GVYYmbcabIIw.content:
Parents who have just arrived in Greece all run into the same questions: which documents are needed, how to find a school nearby, and what support there is for children who don’t speak Greek yet. Here’s the process, step by step.
Documents. In most cases you’ll need your child’s birth certificate with a translation, proof of address, a health record listing vaccinations, and a document showing the parents’ legal residence. If one of them is missing, don’t put off applying: schools usually accept the child and give you time to bring it later.
Choosing a school. Children are enrolled at the school for the area where they live, so there usually isn’t much choice. You can find your school through the municipality or simply ask your neighbours. In big cities, many schools run reception classes for children who don’t speak Greek.
![](https://www.datocms-assets.com/235568/1791140488-img_4939.jpeg)

Language support. The first year is the hardest, and that’s normal. Children attend regular lessons with their class and spend a few hours a week learning Greek separately. Families in our community find that after six months most children chat freely with their classmates.
If you’re turned down. This can happen because classes are full or because of a misunderstanding about documents. In that case, contact the education department of your municipality or write to us — there are people in the community who go with families to appointments and help with interpreting on the spot.

LwzN9PvkSA-QCsM9NVYp3w.title: Enrolment opens at the Ukrainian studies school in Athens
LwzN9PvkSA-QCsM9NVYp3w.content:
The Ukrainian studies school in Athens has opened enrolment for the new school year. This is the fourth intake since the school was set up within the community, and for the first time classes will run twice a week instead of once.
The programme covers Ukrainian language, literature, history and culture for children aged six to fifteen. Groups are formed by age and language level: one set for children who speak Ukrainian at home, and another for those who were born in Greece or arrived very young and learn Ukrainian as a second language.
Classes take place on Saturday mornings and Wednesday afternoons at a cultural centre in the city centre. Each lesson lasts forty-five minutes, with a break in between, and parents usually wait in the hall next door — for many families it has become a weekly meeting point.
You can enrol your child until the end of the month. Just fill in a form with your child’s age and previous schooling — this is only so we can place children in the right group. No prior preparation is needed.

SaO4yMY7QjeK1hnSizDQVQ.name: Trembita Society for the Support and Development of Cultural Heritage
SaO4yMY7QjeK1hnSizDQVQ.summary: A cultural heritage society and Ukrainian Saturday school. Since 2011: education, ensembles, theatre and the festivals “Colors of Pysanka” and “Ukrainian Christmas in Athens”.
SaO4yMY7QjeK1hnSizDQVQ.head: Alla Lobach
SaO4yMY7QjeK1hnSizDQVQ.facts:
Founded: 2011, Athens
Re-registered: 2014 (renamed in 2019)
Chair of the society and head of the school: Alla Lobach
SaO4yMY7QjeK1hnSizDQVQ.content:
The Trembita Society for the Support and Development of Cultural Heritage is one of the liveliest centres of Ukrainian life in Greece. Founded in Athens in 2011 (officially re-registered in 2014 and renamed in 2019), the society has become a true cultural bridge between Ukraine and the cradle of ancient civilisation.

It is led by Alla Lobach, chair of the society and head of the school, who has brought together a team of like-minded people, pupils and parents around shared values.

## Education: the heart of the community

The society’s main educational foundation is the Trembita Ukrainian Saturday School. It started out as a Sunday school more than ten years ago and has since built a structured learning programme.

- Academic grounding: for many years the school worked with the International Ukrainian School of Ukraine’s Ministry of Education, and today it works closely with the “European Collegium” International School, so children receive a high standard of Ukrainian education.
- Language courses: Ukrainian as a foreign language for both adults and schoolchildren.
- Learning by doing: pupils regularly go on hikes, visit archaeological sites and museums across Greece, and take part in sports competitions, charity fairs and themed raffles. In the warmer months the society runs summer camps for children and young people.

## Creativity, stage and keeping traditions alive

Trembita’s cultural life spans generations and art forms:

- Dance and song: the Edelweiss vocal and dance ensemble (formerly the youth group Horobyna), the adult dance ensemble Chervoni Korali and the vocal ensemble Melodzvin.
- Art and stage: the creative space of the ARTTREMBITA studio and Iryna Boiko’s theatre studio.
- Literature and film: poetry and conversation clubs, the annual Shevchenko Days, art and photo exhibitions, book launches and publications.

## Cultural diplomacy and new projects

Trembita keeps bringing Ukrainian words and images into Greek life, and has often been the first to open new doors.

- Signature festivals: founding and running the international events “Colors of Pysanka” and “Children of the World Dance and Sing for Peace”, as well as the family celebration “Ukrainian Christmas in Athens”.
- Pioneers in the arts: the society organised the first large Ukrainian Film Night in Athens, a series of screenings of contemporary documentaries and feature films, and a joint exhibition of Ukrainian and Greek artists at the Melina Cultural Centre.
- Literary achievements: presenting Ukrainian books as part of “Athens — World Book Capital” and translating Lesya Ukrainka’s drama “The Forest Song”.

## Integration and solidarity

The organisation is an important public voice for Ukrainians in the Greek capital. The society is actively involved in:

- the Migrants’ Forum of Athens and Melissa Network for Women;
- the Migrant Integration Council of the City of Athens;
- the Council of Civil Society Organisations of the Municipality of Peristeri;
- charity and social projects of the Κιβωτός του Κόσμου (Ark of the World) foundation.

Since 2022, Trembita has been one of the driving forces behind the creation and growth of the United Ukrainian Diaspora in Greece, coordinating aid, cultural resistance and community unity.

## Powered by enthusiasm

The society runs entirely on the dedication and energy of Ukrainians — it receives no financial support from the host country. Its biggest challenge today is finding a permanent, properly equipped space for the school, rehearsals of the dance and vocal ensembles, and workshops.

Despite every difficulty, Trembita keeps sounding in the very centre of Athens — a symbol of the strength of our roots and a heartfelt love of Ukrainian culture.

dHa4SKC1RHOCFh8ASJEolw.summary: A Saturday school for children aged 4–15: language, literature, history, theatre and dance. It is also home to the only Ukrainian library on Crete.
dHa4SKC1RHOCFh8ASJEolw.facts:
Founded: 2022
School year: 1 November to 30 April, every Saturday
Pupils: children aged 4–15, three age groups
dHa4SKC1RHOCFh8ASJEolw.content:
The Ukrainian Saturday school in Heraklion was founded in 2022. It helps Ukrainian children living on Crete keep their language, culture and connection with Ukraine.

The school teaches children aged 4 to 15 in three age groups: younger, middle and older.

## Every Saturday children learn

- Ukrainian language and literature;
- the history, geography and traditions of Ukraine;
- drama;
- dance;
- art and other creative subjects.

The school year runs from 1 November to 30 April.

## School life

Twice a year — at Christmas and Easter — the pupils put on big celebrations for the Ukrainian community of Crete, along with plays based on Ukrainian classics.

Pupils take part in local festivals and celebrations, presenting Ukrainian culture, travel around Crete and join environmental initiatives such as clearing plastic from beaches.

The school is also home to the only Ukrainian library on Crete, open to both children and adults.

## Our aim

To help children growing up far from Ukraine keep the Ukrainian language, culture and traditions, and a sense of connection with their country.

cGkVeor0TvqCtABEHdP0qw.summary: An NGO that grew out of a women’s initiative started in 2017: psychological support, preventing violence, education, rights advocacy, culture and programmes for children.
cGkVeor0TvqCtABEHdP0qw.head: Hanna Oliinych
cGkVeor0TvqCtABEHdP0qw.facts:
Women’s initiative: since 2017
Legally registered: 2025
Chair: Hanna Oliinych
cGkVeor0TvqCtABEHdP0qw.content:
The Union of Ukrainian Women in Greece is a non-profit organisation whose work goes back to a women’s initiative started in 2017. The organisation was legally registered in 2025.

The Union supports Ukrainian women, children and families in Greece, helping them settle in, grow and take an active part in public life — while staying connected with Ukraine, its language, culture and national heritage.

Our aim is to create opportunities for women to fulfil their potential, become independent and grow, combining psychological and social support with rights advocacy, education, professional development and a stronger community.

## Main areas of work

**Psychological support for women.** Individual consultations and group sessions with psychologists, psychological support and peer support programmes. Support for women living with the consequences of war, forced displacement, violence and other hardships, helping them rebuild their inner strength and self-confidence.

**Preventing and responding to gender-based and domestic violence.** Awareness-raising events and practical training, preparing community navigators and supporting women who have experienced violence. Help with getting legal and psychological support, finding safe accommodation and shelters, and contacting the police, social and specialist services. Working with professionals and institutions in a way that respects each woman’s safety, confidentiality, needs and decisions.

**Social and humanitarian support.** Helping Ukrainians facing hardship, especially people forced to leave Ukraine because of the war. Collecting and delivering humanitarian aid, involving volunteers, sharing information about available services and helping people adapt to life in Greece.

**Education and professional development.** Greek language courses, practical training, workshops, educational and professional meetups. Training in entrepreneurship and starting and growing a business, developing professional skills, preparing for employment and supporting women’s economic independence.

**Rights and advocacy.** Informing women about their rights and opportunities in Greece and representing their needs and interests in dialogue with government bodies, municipalities and international organisations. Promoting equal opportunities, fighting discrimination and helping women take part in decisions that affect their lives.

**Charity and support for Ukraine.** Organising charity events and fundraisers and supporting initiatives that help Ukrainians affected by the war, including the “Titans Under Sail” project. Bringing together the community, volunteers and partners to help those who need it.

**Culture and Ukrainian identity.** Organising concerts, festivals, creative meetups, cultural and arts events. Supporting Ukrainian artists, promoting the Ukrainian language, traditions and heritage, presenting Ukrainian culture in Greece and building Ukrainian-Greek and intercultural dialogue.

**Children and young people.** Educational, creative and wellbeing programmes; organising and coordinating children’s camps, excursions and trips. Supporting children from Ukrainian families in Greece and children coming from Ukraine, especially from communities affected by the war. Creating opportunities for them to grow, make friends and keep their Ukrainian identity.

**Community and volunteering.** Supporting women’s initiatives and leadership and encouraging civic and volunteer involvement. Building peer support communities, sharing useful information and bringing people together around common causes.

Our main audience is Ukrainian women, children and families living in Greece, especially those forced to leave Ukraine because of the war. Some events and programmes are also open to women from other communities.

## Cooperation and partnerships

The Union works with Ukrainian and Greek civil society organisations, migrant communities, municipalities, educational and cultural institutions, social services and international partners.

Through this cooperation we attract resources, run joint initiatives and widen the community’s access to support and opportunities. The Union also builds international partnerships and takes part in preparing and running grant-funded projects.

## Values and approach

Our work is grounded in respect for human dignity, solidarity, integrity and equal opportunities. We pay special attention to every woman’s right to safety, independence and the freedom to shape her own future.

The Union’s strength is its direct connection with the Ukrainian community in Greece. Our work is built on understanding women’s needs and experiences and on their active involvement in creating and running our initiatives. Women take part as participants, volunteers, organisers and leaders, sharing their knowledge and supporting one another.

Ukrainian identity is an inseparable part of our mission. Through cultural initiatives, support for artists and work with children, the Union preserves our national heritage and makes Ukrainian culture visible in Greece — while also helping Ukrainians integrate into local society and building understanding between communities.

The Union of Ukrainian Women in Greece combines help in difficult times with creating opportunities to grow, protecting rights and supporting women’s active participation in society.

Bg3xyLp7Q5SCgoTvPRhAwQ.summary: Monthly discussions of books in Ukrainian and meetings with writers. The club was founded by the writer Nataliia Dovhopol in 2023.
Bg3xyLp7Q5SCgoTvPRhAwQ.head: Nataliia Dovhopol
Bg3xyLp7Q5SCgoTvPRhAwQ.facts:
Founded: 2023, Athens
Founder: writer Nataliia Dovhopol
Meetings: monthly
Participation: free
As of September 2026: around 30 book discussions and 10 meetings with writers
Bg3xyLp7Q5SCgoTvPRhAwQ.content:
The Ukrainian reading club in Athens, “Βιβλιοθεραπεία” (Bibliotherapy), was founded in 2023 by the writer Nataliia Dovhopol.

Members choose books to read together and meet once a month to discuss them. So far the club has mostly read contemporary Ukrainian authors, both fiction and popular non-fiction, but any book written in or translated into Ukrainian is welcome — in print, as an e-book or as an audiobook.

The club also hosts meetings with Ukrainian writers, in person and online, as well as creative writing sessions.

As of September 2026, the club has held around 30 book discussions and 10 meetings with writers.

## How to join

Send us a private message and we’ll be happy to invite you to the next meeting! Taking part is free.

Members help host the events and decide together where and when to meet.

Nef7J7U4RM25qSvLAtqduQ.name: Borysthenes, Greece-Ukraine Business Hub
Nef7J7U4RM25qSvLAtqduQ.subtitle: ΑΜΚΕ «Βορυσθένης, Greece-Ukraine Business Hub»
Nef7J7U4RM25qSvLAtqduQ.summary: A non-profit NGO founded in 2016: it tells Greek society about Ukraine and strengthens cultural, economic and tourism ties between the two countries.
Nef7J7U4RM25qSvLAtqduQ.content:
Borysthenes is a non-profit non-governmental organisation founded in 2016.

## Main goals

- Telling Greek society about Ukraine through the website ukranorama.gr.
- Strengthening friendly, economic, trade, tourism and cultural ties between Ukraine and Greece.
- Supporting the intellectual, cultural and social development of Ukrainians living in Greece and anyone else interested.
- Supporting Ukrainians living in Greece.

## Projects

- “Ukraine as a destination” — facebook.com/OukraniaProorismi
- Bilingual guidebooks “Greek Streets of Kyiv” and “Greek Streets of Odesa” — facebook.com/GreekAddressesUkraine

## The women’s community

In 2017, the community “Ukrainian Women in Greece” was set up as part of Borysthenes. Its main goal was to support Ukrainian women facing hardship, to stand against all forms of violence and to provide psychological help. The community organised many festivals and projects, including the “Festival of Cossack Art” and “Vyshyvanka Day”.

Over time the initiative grew into an organisation of its own: in 2025 the NGO “Union of Ukrainian Women in Greece” was registered.

In recent years Borysthenes has not been actively running projects, but its founders remain committed supporters of the United Ukrainian Diaspora in Greece.

CjISKUaWQsW2mU7t9X2CXQ.summary: “Living Greek”: break through the language barrier, understand spoken Greek and speak naturally. Two groups — A1–A2 and B1–B2+, every Wednesday at 4 Feron Street.

Beginners (A1–A2): Wednesday, 17:30–19:00
Advanced (B1–B2+): Wednesday, 19:00–20:30
Price: €40 per month

CjISKUaWQsW2mU7t9X2CXQ.content:
Want to finally speak Greek the way Greeks actually speak it on the street, not the way it’s written in textbooks? Ukrainians in Athens are welcome to join our “Living Greek” conversation club.

Here we don’t just study grammar — we break through the language barrier, learn to understand real spoken Greek and speak naturally, confidently and with feeling.

## Your host

Iryna Boiko is a director and the founder of a theatre in Athens with 25 years of experience, and teaches acting and stage speech to Greek students. She knows everything about finding your voice, losing the fear of making mistakes and sounding convincing.

## Groups

- Beginners (A1–A2) — a confident start, basic everyday phrases and getting over the fear of speaking. Wednesday, 17:30–19:00.
- Advanced (B1–B2+) — free discussion, slang, idioms, the finer points of intonation and listening. Wednesday, 19:00–20:30.

Where: Information Centre, 4 Feron Street (Victoria Square). Price: €40 per month. To sign up or find out more, send us a private message or call +30 697 363 1659 or +30 694 820 6258.
